summary: Eric Langford’s final internal training deck translates formulation requests into priced development scopes. The personal laptop copy retains informal speaker notes and distinguishes exploratory screens from locked-process commitments.

properties.title: Development handoff: scope the decision first
properties.subject: Internal accounts training | Eric Langford, Early Development Accounts Lead | 09/15/2021 | Personal working copy
properties.keywords: Vehicle ladder; Excipient compatibility screen; early CMC

slides.title: Development handoff: scope the decision first
slides.subtitle: Internal accounts training | Eric Langford, Early Development Accounts Lead | 09/15/2021 | Personal working copy | Durnesswick Laboratories Inc

slides.title: Start with the client’s decision
bullets: Ask what the material must do at the next scale gate.
A dose vehicle, pilot-lot preparation and storage claim are different deliverables.
Write the decision before listing the formulation set.
slides.notes: EL laptop copy. Keep this on the call sheet; we can quote a long experiment list and still miss the decision.

rows: Vehicle ladder at agreed loading and dilution conditions
A solution for every dosing use
Excipient compatibility screen with defined observations
Preparation and handoff with an explicit scale gate

slides.title: Vehicle ladder: scope ingredients
bullets: Target concentration in mg/mL and acceptable dosage form.
Dilution medium, hold condition and observation points.
Preparation quantities and material allowance for repeats.
slides.notes: Ask Julia Carver whether the concentration makes sense before fixing the offer. Clear stock is not necessarily usable dose.

slides.title: Excipient compatibility screen: name the comparison
bullets: Agree candidate excipients and material condition.
Specify the physical or chemical changes to examine.
Separate a screening observation from a finished-product specification.

slides.title: Exploratory wording; process wording
bullets: Compare recipes under agreed screen conditions.
Recommend a formulation set for follow-up.
Document visible handling limitations.
bullets_right: Establish reproducible preparation at agreed scale.
Set acceptance criteria when the evidence supports them.

slides.title: Price the work creating the answer
bullets: Include receipt, preparation, observation and interpretation.
Include screen suitability checks and ambiguity-resolving repeats.
Treat new loading, extra excipients or extended hold as scope changes.
slides.notes: No example fee here. Build the priced scope with the scientific owner; explain what the fee covers.

slides.title: Material request before the offer leaves
bullets: Ask for identity, physical form and available mass.
Ask whether another material lot will be used for dosing.
Reserve material for follow-up rather than consuming it all in the broad screen.

rows: Does the scope answer the decision?
Can the formulation set be made from available material?
What must the receiving team reproduce?

slides.title: Change control without a surprise invoice
bullets: State assumptions in the offer.
Agree changed work when intended use changes.
Offer a clear choice between a smaller answer and expanded scope.
slides.notes: My reminder: call first. A tidy development note does not cure an unagreed extension.

slides.title: Accounts exercise
bullets: Hypothetical request: a clear preparation for dilution into aqueous dosing medium.
Explain why concentrate clarity alone is insufficient.
Draft dilution, recipe-card and recommendation deliverables; keep process lock separate.
slides.notes: Let colleagues answer before showing the dilution point. No client data in this training copy.

slides.title: Before sending the priced scope
bullets: Decision and intended use appear first.
Material, conditions and deliverables match the scientific owner’s plan.
Exploratory claims, transfer responsibilities and change triggers are clear.
slides.notes: Retained langforde laptop working copy. Use these questions, not this deck, as the client attachment.
